newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Crucial Venezuelan airline Viasa meeting now Feb 8.
newsitem.headline: Crucial Venezuelan airline Viasa meeting now Feb 8.

text.p: A crucial meeting between shareholders of struggling Venezuelan airline Viasa has been moved to February 8 to give workers enough time to consider the latest restructuring proposal, sources said.
The meeting had been set for January 31. But "as we now need to know the workers' position (on the proposal) ... yesterday we decided to move the meeting to February 8," Viasa sources told Reuters.

Spain's Iberia, which owns a 45 percent share in the Venezuelan flag carrier, reached a preliminary agreement late on Tuesday with Venezuela's Investment Fund (FIV) to save the airline from bankruptcy. Now the future of the airline is in its workers' hands, Iberia said.
Iberia and the FIV will each inject some $25 million -- contingent on workers accepting a restructuring plan that would cut some 20 percent of jobs, freeze wages and suspend unprofitable routes.

Viasa suspended all flights February 23, shortly after workers had rejected a previous cost-cutting plan. The FIV owns 40 percent of the airline, which employs 2,200. Venezuela's largest bank, Banco Provincial owns the remaining 15 percent.
